lesson.intro: Sebuah teks bisa memuat informasi yang keliru lalu diperbaiki. Soal sering memakai pengecoh dari bagian lama. Tugasmu adalah mengikuti informasi yang paling baru dan benar.

sections.heading: Penanda koreksi
sections.bodyMd: Kata seperti **actually** dan **rather** sering menandai koreksi. Penulis juga bisa memakai **mistaken** untuk mengakui kesalahan sebelumnya, atau **retract** untuk menarik pernyataan.

sections.heading: Pengecoh
sections.bodyMd: Sebuah **distractor** biasanya memakai kata dari teks, tetapi maknanya salah. Hati-hati dengan pilihan yang hanya mengulang informasi lama, karena itu sudah **amend** atau diganti.

sections.heading: Revisi dan pembaruan
sections.bodyMd: Penulis melakukan **revision** atau **update** untuk memperbaiki data. Jika teks menyebut perbaikan, anggap versi itu yang berlaku. Jangan salah paham dengan versi lama yang sudah diganti.

formulas.label: Revisi
formulas.pattern: amend / update → versi terbaru yang berlaku

formulas.label: Cek
formulas.pattern: apakah informasi ini versi lama atau versi baru?

block3.title: Koreksi pada Artikel Museum
block3.text:
The museum newsletter published an article last month about the bronze statue in the east hall. The article stated that the statue dated from the twelfth century. Actually, the statue is much newer. A correction is needed, because several visitors and teachers have repeated the mistaken date.

The error began with a label. The old label was printed in a catalogue that many people used. Visitors may misunderstand the label as the official date, but it was only a draft. The curator explained that the team did not check the original records before the catalogue was printed.

A distractor in the old display made the problem worse. A small card beside the statue listed a second date, which was rather different from the first one. This card was meant to show a different object, but many visitors read it as the same item. The museum has now removed the card.

The new date is based on metal analysis and records from the archive. These records show that the statue was cast in the fifteenth century. The staff will amend the catalogue, the online guide, and the wall label. Each change will appear in the next revision of the guide, which is due in June.

Some readers asked why the museum did not retract the whole article. The editor's answer was that only the date was wrong. The rest of the article, including the description of the craftsmanship, remains accurate. Retracting everything would have been unnecessary, and it would have confused readers who had already learned the correct details.

The editor also thanked the readers who pointed out the mistake. Their feedback helped the team update the records faster than planned. The museum will publish a short note in each issue for the next six months, so that people can follow the changes.

Finally, the staff asked visitors to check the newest version of the guide before they repeat the old date in a school project or an online post. A correction is only useful if people see it, and the team hopes this notice will reach the people who first read the mistake. The staff also placed a copy of the notice beside the statue, so that visitors who had read the old card would see the new information.
